audits.title: Audit on antipsychotic prescribing in children and young people with a learning disability under the care of mental health services in Surrey
audits.standard: NICE guidelines on antipsychotic prescribing in learning disability
audits.setting: CAMHS, Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Reasons for starting documented for all 5 on antipsychotics; for 4 started over 12 months ago, no documentation of side effect, EPSE, weight, blood pressure, glycaemic or lipid monitoring; 1 lacked a 6-monthly review.

audits.other_findings: Reviews in 3 patients did not consider dose reduction or stopping; lack of awareness of NICE guidance noted.
audits.citation: James T, Zainab A, Mura S, Vallance A, Okusi D. Audit on antipsychotic prescribing in children and young people with a learning disability under the care of mental health services in Surrey. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S71-S71.

audits.title: Audit on use of PRN (pro re nata) psychotropic medication for behavioural disturbance in individuals with intellectual disability in the community
audits.standard: Standards for PRN psychotropic protocols for behavioural disturbance (protocol accessible, indications, de-escalation, maximum dose, recording)
audits.setting: Community intellectual disability service, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board

cycle1.result: Medical file standards 100% achieved; PRN protocol standards achieved in only 53% of cases.

audits.other_findings: Gaps included descriptions of when to use PRN, non-drug de-escalation, expected effect, minimum interval between doses and 24-hour maximum dose.
audits.citation: Dhandapani A, Soundararajan S, Jones C. Audit on use of PRN (pro re nata) psychotropic medication for behavioural disturbance in individuals with intellectual disability in the community. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S75-S76.

audits.title: Audit of Prescribing Practices & Medication Monitoring on Learning Disability Female Low Secure Unit
audits.standard: Trust and national guidelines on psychotropic prescribing and monitoring (indications on drug chart, HDAT/combined antipsychotic care plans, consent to treatment and capacity forms, annual health check, blood monitoring, annual valproate risk acknowledgement form).
audits.setting: Learning disability female low secure forensic unit, Coventry and Warwickshire Partnership NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 100% compliance for indications on drug chart, HDAT/combined antipsychotic care plans, consent to treatment forms, annual health check and psychotropic blood monitoring; MHA capacity assessment form 71%; annual valproate risk acknowledgement form in women of childbearing age 0%.

audits.other_findings: Investigation results were hard to locate. Recommendations: care plans for all patients on valproate with review dates for risk acknowledgement forms and consistent filing of results.
audits.citation: England R, Rashid A. Audit of Prescribing Practices & Medication Monitoring on Learning Disability Female Low Secure Unit. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(Suppl 1):S156-S157.

audits.title: Audit of Patients Prescribed Psychotropic Medication in the Community Learning Disabilities Psychiatry Services of the Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
audits.standard: NHS England STOMP (Stopping Overmedication of People with a Learning Disability, Autism or Both) recommendations
audits.setting: Four Community Learning Disabilities locality teams, Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Good evidence of capacity, consent, best interests, MDT input and regular review of medication, side effects and response (no figures given); rationale for off-label use could be recorded more clearly.

audits.other_findings: Twenty patients were randomly selected per team, excluding those not on psychotropics. Psychotropics still play a significant role in managing behavioural problems.
audits.citation: Adetoki A. Audit of Patients Prescribed Psychotropic Medication in the Community Learning Disabilities Psychiatry Services of the Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S123-S123. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.336.

audits.title: Clinical Audit of Psychotropic Medication Use in People With Learning Disabilities and Behaviour That Challenges
audits.setting: Chester-le-Street Adult Learning Disability Community Team

cycle1.result: Rationale documented 100%; used with psychological interventions 100%; comorbidities identified 100%; review within 3-4 weeks 20%; treatment duration documented 0%; patient/carer involvement 40%; MDT review within 3 months 40%.

audits.other_findings: Recommendations: standardised early reviews, documentation of duration, carer engagement and timely MDT reviews.
audits.citation: Olajolumo J, Ogar I. Clinical Audit of Psychotropic Medication Use in People With Learning Disabilities and Behaviour That Challenges. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S265-S265. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10649.

audits.title: Audit Review of Psychotropic Medication of the Caerphilly Psychiatry Community Learning Disability Caseload
audits.standard: NICE and Royal College of Psychiatrists guidance on regular review and documentation of indication
audits.setting: Community learning disability psychiatry service, Caerphilly

cycle1.result: 114 (97.4%) on at least one psychotropic; 77 (65.8%) on antipsychotics. Indication: clear mental health diagnosis 23/77 (29.9%), behaviours that challenge 15 (19.5%), no clear indication 39 (50.6%). Antidepressants (44): no documented indication in 8 (18.2%).

audits.other_findings: 47 (61.0%) on antipsychotic doses at or below 25% BNF maximum. Medication increased in 27 (23.1%) and reduced in 23 (19.7%).
audits.citation: Lin M, Swift A, Medhurst D. Audit Review of Psychotropic Medication of the Caerphilly Psychiatry Community Learning Disability Caseload. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S316-S316. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11671.

audits.title: POMHS 9b - antipsychotic prescribing in people with a learning disability.
audits.standard: POMH-UK 9b: indication documented (Deb 2006); continuing need reviewed at least annually (Deb 2006); annual side-effect review including EPS and 4 aspects of metabolic syndrome (NICE CG82, 2009)
audits.setting: 7 clinical teams in Essex and Bedfordshire & Luton, South Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust (POMH-UK programme)

cycle1.result: Standard 1 100%; Standard 2 over 90%; Standard 3 lower than at re-audit (figures not given).

cycle2.result: Standard 1 maintained 100%; Standard 2 over 90%; Standard 3 improved from baseline.

audits.other_findings: Analysis and benchmarking done centrally by POMH-UK with an individual Trust report.
audits.citation: Thalitaya MD, Udu V, Nicholls M, Clark T, Prasher VP. POMHS 9b - antipsychotic prescribing in people with a learning disability. Psychiatr Danub. 2011;23 Suppl 1:S50-6. PMID: 21894103.

audits.title: Quality of prescribing of antipsychotic medication for people with intellectual disability under the care of UK mental health services: a cross-sectional audit of clinical practice.
audits.standard: Practice standards derived from evidence-based guidelines including NICE (indications and annual side-effect screening)
audits.setting: 54 UK mental health services (Royal College of Psychiatrists quality improvement programme)

cycle1.result: 64% prescribed antipsychotics; annual screening documented for body weight 41%, blood pressure 32%, and blood glucose and lipids 37%.

audits.other_findings: Screening varied widely between services (0-100%); most prescribing was for licensed or evidence-based indications.
audits.citation: Paton C, Bhatti S, Purandare K, Roy A, Barnes T. Quality of prescribing of antipsychotic medication for people with intellectual disability under the care of UK mental health services: a cross-sectional audit of clinical practice. BMJ Open. 2016;6(12):e013116. doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2016-013116. PMID: 27920085.

audits.title: Clinical audit of psychotropic medication use at a South African intellectual disability hospital.
audits.standard: World Psychiatric Association and NICE guidance on psychotropic use in intellectual disability
audits.setting: Outpatient department, specialist intellectual disability psychiatric hospital, Cape Town

cycle1.result: 88% prescribed psychotropics; antipsychotics were over half of prescriptions, often for behaviour that challenges without psychosis; low effective doses used.

audits.other_findings: Gaps in documentation of rationale, review scheduling, side-effect monitoring and consistent use of behavioural strategies.
audits.citation: Akpabio IU, Smith P, Kleintjes S. Clinical audit of psychotropic medication use at a South African intellectual disability hospital. S Afr J Psychiatr. 2026;32:2553. doi:10.4102/sajpsychiatry.v32i0.2553. PMID: 41646454.
